title: Aelius Aristides, Platonic orations: Or. 2 To Plato: In Defence of Oratory; Or. 3 In Defence of the Four; Or. 4 To Capito / Элий Аристид, Против Платона
author: Aelius Aristides
size: Or. 2 and Or. 3 are very long; estimated 70,000–80,000 words in total. Or. 4 is short (about 4,000).
ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Элий Аристид': Mezheritskaya covers the Sacred Tales, To Rome, funeral orations and monodies, the Egyptian and Smyrnaean orations and the hymns. Aristeas adds minor pieces. Or. 2–4 are not listed.
en_evidence: Behr, Complete Works I (Brill 1986); Trapp, Loeb (2017 for Or. 1–2, 2021 for Or. 3–4). Cited from memory and not re-checked online.
other_translations: Italian and French versions of Or. 2 exist (not re-verified).
value: The fullest ancient reply to Plato's Gorgias: a defence of rhetoric and of Pericles, Miltiades, Cimon and Themistocles. Central for the rhetoric–philosophy quarrel and for Platonism in the Second Sophistic.
ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Long, periodic Atticist argument with many quotations from Plato. Can be cross-checked against Behr and Trapp.
pilot_unit: Or. 4 To Capito (short, self-contained), then Or. 2 §§1–100.
